units.title: Ethereum mainnet reference and cross-chain deployment parity
angles: Arithmetic and control flow. Read the interpreter this network runs at the release its endpoint reports, and any compiler, bytecode rewriting, caching or code analysis stage in front of it. Cover the 256 bit integer library and its pinned version, MULMOD, ADDMOD, DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SIGNEXTEND, SAR, SHL, SHR, BYTE, EXP, the comparisons, JUMP and JUMPI with the jump destination analysis, KECCAK256, MCOPY, memory expansion and CALLDATALOAD. Compare each with the Ethereum specification at the edges that OPCODES.md lists, and read the release notes and fix commits since the versions OPCODES.md records. Then rerun the scripts in research/network-risk/tools/opdiff (battery.py, targeted.py, pmdiff.py, pmdiff2.py, swaps.py, replay.py) for this unit's chain ids, write the outputs into your work directory, and add vectors for anything the reading makes suspicious. Report every result that differs from the specification, every release that changed these paths, how a wrong result would change the pool math in src/libraries (TickMath, BitMath, FullMath, SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, TickBitmap) or the logic that depends on it, and which validators could run a different code path than the public endpoint.

Upcoming forks. Assume every network upgrade scheduled or proposed for the next six months ships. What changes for the PoolManager and for funds already inside it, and what could an ordinary account do the day after?

code.title: MegaETH, HyperEVM and Monad: PoolManager code their block producers have never executed, and what a wrong word there would pay out of the shared balance
code.task: The build of this checkout is in research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json (runtime 24,009 bytes), research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/pyevm.py is a reference EVM in Python, research/network-risk/tools/opdiff/v4math.py is a transcription of the math libraries, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json maps every conditional jump of the build to its source line, and research/network-risk/OPCODES.md holds what is already tested and read, with sections on what cycles 10 to 38 added and a list of what is not covered. Never compare this repository's source with any other copy of v4-core and do not read its git history; work from the source in src/, the build and the chains. Read-only RPC only, no transactions. Do not install software. Python 3, rustc 1.97 with cargo, go 1.24, node and the system C and C++ compilers are present, and you may compile downloaded source inside your own work directory. Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Record every sampling seed, save every mismatch record in full, and bracket each batch of calls to a public endpoint with web3_clientVersion so the build that answered is known. If an endpoint refuses your client (HTTP 403, 429 or a challenge page), record that and use another public endpoint; do not try to get around the refusal and use no API keys. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1352 and L-1353. Three networks have a block producer whose code is not what eth_call runs or cannot be read: MegaETH's closed compiler-based executor, HyperEVM's closed validator, and Monad's native compiled code. Cycles 30 to 38 established which PoolManager sites each has never executed with a wide operand: the fee mulDiv of SwapMath (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:64-65), the wide branches of SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta (:208-209 and :250-252), the fee copy of Position (src/libraries/Position.sol:94-96), donate and exact-output swaps on some of them. OPCODES.md sets these aside for two reasons: only a pool the attacker creates reaches them, and a wide amount cannot be settled. The cycle 38 critic points out that neither reason is enough. All pools of a currency are paid from one balance (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), so a wrong result in a pool the attacker created from two currencies that other pools hold would be paid with other LPs' funds; and the cycle 38 answer to L-1333 reached the fee site on HyperEVM in existing pools with an amount that settles. This theme does not look for a producer fault; no evidence of one exists. It works out, per site, whether an ordinary account can put the producer on code it has never run with a result that reaches the shared balance, so that the remaining exposure is stated exactly. Monad's shipped emitter has run every one of these sites in the model (cycles 31 to 37), so for Monad the question is only which sites still lack a mined run. Scripts and data: research/network-risk/cycles/034/theme-first-inputs-and-stale-sync.work/scripts (bounds.py, wide.py, pools.py, monadpools.py, cost.py), research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-hyperevm-producer-census.work/scripts (wide34.py, inv.py, census.py, shape_tracer.js) and its per-pc tables, research/network-risk/cycles/038/hyperevm.work/scripts (l1333.py, pools38.py), research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-closed-producer-operand-census.work/scripts (pmsites.py, pminv.py), research/network-risk/cycles/030/theme-monad-mined-native-coverage.work/scripts (classify30.py, analyze30.py), tools/opdiff/v4math.py and pyevm.py, opcodes/jumpmap.json. Disk space is short: keep counts, not raw traces. Task 1 (L-1352): for each never-run site list, from src/, the exact condition under which it is entered (which product must reach 2^256, which amount, which liquidity and price distance) and the cheapest way an ordinary account can meet it: in an existing pool with real liquidity, or in a hookless pool it creates from two currencies that other pools already hold, with tick spacing, price, position and amount chosen freely. Give the cost in tokens and gas, and say whether the call completes or must revert later (the int128 casts at src/libraries/Pool.sol:452-458 and in SafeCast, the price limit, the delta check at the end of unlock). Task 2: for each site that can complete, follow the result word forward to every place it reaches: amountIn, amountOut and feeAmount of the step (SwapMath), amountCalculated and amountSpecifiedRemaining, feeGrowthGlobal (src/libraries/Pool.sol:404-405 and :446), protocol fees, the swap delta the caller must settle or may take, and a position's owed fees through fee growth inside. Write, per site, which single wrong word (too large, too small, by how much) would let the caller take more of a currency than it paid, or credit its own position with fees nobody paid, and through which line that reaches the shared balance. Sites where every wrong word ends in a revert or a loss for the caller only are recorded as such. Task 3: run each completing reach by eth_call with state overrides through the deployed PoolManager on MegaETH (mainnet.megaeth.com and any endpoint of a stateless validator), HyperEVM (official endpoint and both replicas) and Monad (the interpreter endpoints), and compare every returned word with pyevm.py. For L-1353 send the 24 wide exact-input swaps of l1333.py against three existing hookless MegaETH pools. Say plainly that this tests replicas and interpreters. Then look for mined evidence: on MegaETH search the validated blocks, and on HyperEVM the replica traces, for any transaction that entered each site with a wide operand inside the PoolManager; on Monad list which of these sites the mined transactions since v0.16.7 have entered. Task 4: state the remaining exposure per network in one table: site, reachable by an ordinary account (existing pool or own pool, cost), result reaches the shared balance (yes with the path, or no), executed by the producer inside the PoolManager (count), executed by the producer in any contract with the same operand shape (count from the censuses), and what an independent node would notice if the producer were wrong there (a changed Swap log changes the receipts root on HyperEVM; MegaETH's validator recomputes the state root; Monad's validators all run the same code). Rewrite the two sentences of OPCODES.md that dismiss these sites so that they say what this table shows; put the proposed wording in your result. Task 5: nothing here is a finding unless a result differs from the reference on a producer, replica or interpreter. A site that an ordinary account can reach today with a result that reaches the shared balance and that the producer has never executed inside the PoolManager is a high-priority lead with the pool, the input and the amounts; say what observation would close it (one mined transaction through the site with a correct result). Send no transaction. Say for the other 18 networks that this theme does not apply.

code.title: Producers without block simulation, and Polygon's parallel executor: transient storage between transactions and between workers

Keep downloads and build output under a directory named build/ or dl/ inside your work directory. Do not download compiler toolchains or other binaries to run them; source archives are fine. Analysis only: no exploit code and no transactions. Leads L-1354, L-1358 and L-1357. Two questions about the lifetime of transient storage rest on reading. First, the official endpoints of Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM and Arc refuse eth_simulateV1, so the multi-transaction scenarios have never run against the code that produces their blocks; that the producers clear transient storage between transactions is known from source (Monad), from the revm version behind replicas (MegaETH, HyperEVM) and from third-party endpoints (Arc). Mined blocks can show it directly: sync is callable without unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) and leaves the synced currency set until the transaction ends, and a native settle in a later transaction reverts if that currency were still set (the check at src/PoolManager.sol:356). Second, Polygon executes the transactions of a block in parallel (BlockSTM) and lets a worker read what another transaction wrote through a multi-version store. If transient storage, or a storage word written and then reverted inside a frame, could be read across transactions through that store, a worker could see another account's open unlock. eth_call never runs in parallel, so no endpoint test covers this. Scripts: research/network-risk/cycles/033/high-throughput.work/scripts/pmtrace.py, research/network-risk/cycles/034/theme-first-inputs-and-stale-sync.work/scripts/stalesync.py, research/network-risk/cycles/034/hyperevm.work/scripts (l1262.py, l1262b.py: receipts of blocks with several PoolManager transactions), research/network-risk/cycles/037/stablecoin-l1.work/scripts (arcreplay.py, arclogs.py), research/network-risk/cycles/037/theme-hyperevm-producer-census.work/scripts, the bor binaries and drivers of research/network-risk/cycles/031/theme-go-family-binary-lift.work and research/network-risk/cycles/033/theme-persistent-storage-binary-lift.work/scripts (stgo2.py ran bor's StateDB and ParallelStateDB with the multi-version store answering not-found). Comparing bor revisions is allowed. Task 1 (L-1354): on Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM and Arc find mined blocks that contain a transaction which calls PoolManager.sync for an ERC-20 and ends without settling it (routers that sync before a transfer and then revert late, Multicall batches, failed swaps), followed in the same block by a PoolManager transaction that settles native value or syncs and settles another currency and succeeds. Use callTracer or replica traces where served and calldata decoding of router and Multicall transactions otherwise. For each network give the number of such pairs found and three examples with block and transaction hashes, or say that none exists and how many blocks were searched.
